prompts.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: 16:9 landscape editorial photograph for an industrial metal bandsaw blade service website. Premium realistic industrial photography, convincing physical engineering, graphite and brushed silver palette with tiny restrained burgundy accents, soft directional light, detailed metal texture, photographic not a render. A single scene, not a collage. Main subject large and clearly recognisable around the center-right (55-65 percent of the frame), upper middle useful for a mobile crop. Left quarter relatively dark and quiet. No text, lettering, logos, watermarks, labels, overlays or UI. No dramatic sci-fi machinery. This is generic illustrative photography, no specific company or factory identity. Scene: a wider three-quarter view of a substantial metal bandsaw blade decoiling and length preparation station in a tidy workshop. A large upright spool of narrow toothed steel strip on the right, one straight strip feeds horizontally across steel guide rollers into a robust precision length cutting fixture; spare neatly wound rolls in soft focus behind. The sharp individual teeth along one edge of the strip are recognisable. Wide industrial composition, no people. The defining subject is the large round steel coil and the feeding rollers, NOT a macro welding clamp or stacked finished sawblade loops.

selectionEdit.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this single industrial measurement photograph. Keep the same two natural hands, workbench, lighting, blade sample and camera composition. Correct only the steel vernier caliper mechanics and placement: its TWO large lower outside-measurement jaws must be closed down to exactly embrace the width of the vertical bandsaw strip, with the fixed left jaw touching the left smooth blade edge and the movable right jaw touching the right toothed blade edge. No air gaps between the measuring faces and the two blade edges. Make it a recognisably correct mechanical vernier caliper with a single fixed jaw and a single sliding jaw, not extra prongs. Keep the bandsaw blade unmoving, the tool held horizontally by the right hand and the blade held by the left hand. Photorealistic, no extra fingers, no logos, no added overlay text. Preserve everything else.
